bugs.name: Creating an organization cleanup rule says it was updated
bugs.summary: The success confirmation for a newly added cleanup rule uses update wording.
bugs.expected: Creating a cleanup rule should show a creation confirmation.
bugs.actual: After Add creates a rule, the confirmation says “Cleanup rule has been updated.”
reproSteps: Create a disposable organization and open Settings > Packages.
Choose Add cleanup rule, select a package type, enable it, and save.
Read the confirmation on the resulting edit page.

bugs.name: Package search field is blank after browser Back restores the query URL
bugs.summary: Browser Back returns to the package-search URL with the prior q parameter, but the Search field remains empty while Cargo stays selected; this persisted after a fresh repeat and a settled-state check.
bugs.expected: After Back returns to the package URL with q=missing-package-example&type=cargo, the Search field should show missing-package-example and the Type filter should show Cargo.
bugs.actual: Back returned to /admin/packages?q=missing-package-example&type=cargo. The Type filter showed Cargo, but the Search field showed its Search... placeholder and was empty.
reproSteps: In a fresh browser, load the authorized administrator session and open /admin/packages.
Enter missing-package-example in the package Search field and press Enter.
Choose Cargo in the Type filter and click the magnifying-glass search button.
Focus the Search field, press Control+A and Backspace to clear it, then click the magnifying-glass search button.
Use browser Back once. Observe the URL /admin/packages?q=missing-package-example&type=cargo, the Cargo Type filter, and the empty Search field showing its placeholder.

bugs.name: Cleanup-rule validation resets the selected package type
bugs.summary: An invalid version regex resets the cleanup rule's selected Type from npm to Alpine. Correcting just the reported regex error then saves a rule for the wrong package type.
bugs.expected: Preserve the chosen package type and all other valid form values after regex validation fails.
bugs.actual: Selecting npm and submitting Keep versions matching '[' displays the invalid-regex error but resets Type to Alpine while retaining '['. Correcting the regex to '^stable$' and submitting creates an Alpine rule. Agent reproduced the reset twice and verified the saved disabled rule.
reproSteps: Sign in and open /user/settings/packages.
Click Add cleanup rule.
Choose Type npm and set Keep versions matching to [.
Click Add.
Observe the regex validation error and that Type has changed to Alpine.
Correct only the regex to ^stable$ and click Add.
Open the saved rule and observe its Type is Alpine instead of npm.

reviewedVariants.name: Invalid cleanup-rule regex resets the selected package type
reviewedVariants.summary: Submitting an invalid cleanup-rule regex resets Cargo to Alpine; correcting only the regex then saves the rule as Alpine.
reviewedVariants.expected: When the invalid regex is rejected, the form should retain Cargo. Correcting the regex and resubmitting without changing Type should create a Cargo rule.
reviewedVariants.actual: The validation error appeared and the form changed Type from Cargo to Alpine while retaining the Keep versions matching value. After I corrected only the regex, the app reported success and showed the rule as Alpine.
reproSteps: Using the authenticated own account momentic-admin session, open /user/settings/packages. The provided saved session was used; no credentials were entered during the flow.
Click Add cleanup rule. Leave Enabled unchecked, choose Cargo in Type, enter mo-account-cleanup-4b7c2e91 in Keep versions matching, and enter [ in Remove versions matching.
Click Add. Observe the regex validation error, Type showing Alpine, and the Keep versions matching value still present.
Without changing Type, replace [ with the valid regex ^$ and click Add. Observe the success message and the resulting edit form showing Type as Alpine.
Click Remove for this uniquely named test rule. Verify the cleanup-rules page reports that there are no cleanup rules.

bugs.name: Packages summary text obscured by cleanup button at narrow viewport
bugs.summary: At 390×844 on the Packages page, the Clean up expired data button visibly covers part of the Manage packages summary, making its total-size text unreadable; the overlap persists after refresh and waiting.
bugs.expected: The Manage packages summary, including package count, total size, and unreferenced size, should remain readable and unobscured by the cleanup button.
bugs.actual: At 390×844, the cleanup button covers the middle/right portion of the first summary line, obscuring the total-size text. The unreferenced-size value remains visible on the next line. The overlap persisted after refreshing and waiting five seconds.
reproSteps: Start with the authorized administrator session (the provided authenticated state was loaded before navigation).
Set the browser viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.
Navigate to /admin, expand Code assets, and select Packages.
On /admin/packages, inspect the Manage packages summary near the top of the page. Do not activate Clean up expired data.
Refresh the page and wait five seconds; the button still obscures the total-size text.

matchingGuidance.acceptanceScope: Accepted as a valid reference by user instruction; source prerequisites and remaining evidence gaps are retained below.
prerequisites: 390px viewport and summary/button widths exceed header width.
